findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the fuse treats non-`exhausted_transient` unhealthy dispositions (`retryable_deferred`, `commit_unknown`) — either fold sleep-cap `retryable_deferred` into the eligible counter or state the normalization guarantee that a truly-stuck transient endpoint eventually surfaces as `exhausted_transient` within the pass — and explicitly list which deferred dispositions neither increment nor reset a scope's counter.
evidence: retry_budget.plan_next_retry returns action='defer' (→ retryable_deferred) when cumulative_sleep_ms+delay_ms > MAX_CUMULATIVE_SLEEP_MS, distinct from action='exhausted'
decide_replay yields Disposition.exhausted_transient ONLY when observation=='old_conclusive' AND budget_remaining is False; other transient paths yield retryable_deferred or commit_unknown
Plan: 'counting only that scope’s eligible exhausted_transient outcomes' with an exclusion list that omits retryable_deferred / commit_unknown / dependency_deferred / scope_deferred
findings.finding: The fuse's eligible-counter set is defined only as `exhausted_transient`, but the retry budget emits a distinct `retryable_deferred` (plan_next_retry action='defer' when the cumulative-sleep cap is hit before MAX_INVOCATIONS) and `commit_unknown`; a persistently rate-limited/slow endpoint can loop producing `retryable_deferred` and never surface `exhausted_transient`, so the endpoint fuse would never trip for that failure mode.
findings.location: Plan 'Fuse counter semantics' (Counted per scope / Thresholds) and step 4 exclusions
scenarios: An endpoint that is consistently rate-limited such that each dispatch hits the sleep-cap deferral rather than fully exhausting physical invocations
A commit-unknown-heavy endpoint (write timeouts) that never yields exhausted_transient

The consecutive-threshold + open + reset-on-success shape is textbook circuit-breaker prior art (retrieved: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuit_breaker_design_pattern; microservices.io/patterns/reliability/circuit-breaker.html — 'When the number of consecutive failures crosses a threshold, the circuit breaker trips').

The plan DOES consider internal prior art (retains/distinguishes classify.check_blast_radius, confirmed at classify.py:305) and reuses operation_outcome.FailureScope + DelaySource.fuse (confirmed in operation_outcome.py), so the gap is narrow: no external prior-art note justifying the bespoke per-scope quorum design over a stock breaker.

findings.finding: The plan introduces a novel 'endpoint-failure scoped fuse' (a circuit-breaker-family mechanism) but never situates its NEW dimensions against the established circuit-breaker pattern or existing breaker libraries; it only distinguishes the internal blast-radius guard.
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer asks why a hand-rolled per-scope counter was built instead of adopting an established resilience breaker.
The quorum thresholds (2 tickets / 2 endpoints) drift from any known breaker semantics without a documented rationale anchor.
findings.suggested_fix: In step 3 or the 'Fuse scope definitions' section, add: 'This fuse is a scoped variant of the standard circuit-breaker pattern; the novelty over a stock breaker is (a) per-(provider,endpoint) attribution keyed on coordinator-held identity rather than diagnostic text, and (b) multi-ticket/multi-endpoint quorum thresholds that let independent scopes continue. An off-the-shelf single-key breaker was not adopted because it cannot express these scope-attributed quorums against the existing FailureScope vocabulary.'
